quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Bicyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are to your left. Parked vehicles are to your right. You should steer:

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
Down the middle, between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle, between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: Steer down the middle between the oncoming cars and parked cars. This gives you the most safety in both directions.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light means:

options.text: The same thing as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same thing as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Go when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: You see heavy smoke covering the road ahead. You should:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
Turn on high beams and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: Slow down right away. Drive as far right as possible and stop off the road. Check if it is safe before driving again. Some smoke can harm your eyes and lungs.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.question: Large trucks are likely to lose speed when:

options.text: Driving up long or steep hills.
Driving in long, gradual curves.
Driving down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to speed up than smaller vehicles. They lose speed going up long or steep hills. Leave extra space behind large trucks, especially on hills.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed and brakes.

questions.question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way, even when you signal.

questions.question: Do not use high beams in fog or mist because:

options.text: The light reflects back into your eyes.
Approaching vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light reflects back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam light bounces back into your eyes. Use low beams instead.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Trucks entering.
Truck exit only.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep downgrade is coming. Check your brakes.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you on a two-lane road:

options.text: Slowly reduce speed to encourage them to pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Brake suddenly, then go back to your original speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce speed to encourage them to pass you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating, slowly reduce your speed. This encourages them to pass you. If you can, change lanes. Never brake suddenly.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads. A solid yellow line means do not pass. A broken yellow line means you may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When passing, return to your original lane when:

options.text: You can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You have cleared the front bumper of the other vehicle.
You are 50 feet in front of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into your lane only when you see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror. This ensures safe distance between your vehicles.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
There is two-way traffic.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you about two-way traffic ahead.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down and proceed with caution at a flashing yellow light. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Be ready to stop if needed.
Keep a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is beyond a hill or around a curve. A vehicle may be stopped just out of sight. Adjust your speed so you can stop if necessary.

questions.question: You should not use your horn:

options.text: When visibility ahead is limited.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Using your horn near a blind pedestrian can be dangerous and may startle them. Yield and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your nerve impulses and body functions. It reduces your ability to focus and stay alert.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege. All drivers must keep roads safe. If you abuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: Your vehicle wheels have gone off the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to get back on the pavement.
Hold the steering wheel firm, release the gas, and gently brake.
Brake hard and turn the wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firm, release the gas, and gently brake.
questions.explanation: Hold the wheel firmly, release the gas, and brake gently. Wait until your speed drops. Check traffic and safely rejoin the road. Do not jerk the wheel—this can cause you to lose control or cross into other lanes.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an upcoming corner. You must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles that are also turning left.
All vehicles coming toward you.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a walk signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other vehicles that have a green light.

questions.question: Vehicles behind a school bus with red flashing lights must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is pulled in.
The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is pulled in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has red flashing lights and the stop arm out, you must stay stopped. Do not move until the lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled in, and the bus starts moving.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, turn into:

options.text: Any lane.
The first lane.
The second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first lane.
questions.explanation: When turning, always turn into the first available legal lane in the direction you are going.

questions.question: A broken yellow center line means:

options.text: You cannot pass.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow center line means you can cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if no traffic is coming. Never cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: You must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address on the vehicle you hit.

questions.question: In a car on a highway, it is:

options.text: Illegal to drink from or have open alcohol containers.
Legal to drink alcohol if you are not driving.
Legal to drink alcohol while driving if you are not drunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Illegal to drink from or have open alcohol containers.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while under the influence of alcohol. No one in the car—drivers or passengers—can have an open alcohol container while the car is running.

questions.question: When your view is blocked at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching an intersection. If you cannot see clearly, stop completely. Then move forward slowly until you can see in both directions.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant that slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slow.

questions.question: If you have a sudden tire blowout, you should:

options.text: Use the brakes lightly.
Pump the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and using light brake pressure.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No passing zone.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Two-way traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: A yellow triangle sign with black letters means no passing zone. It appears on the left side of two-lane roads where you cannot pass.

questions.question: You should increase the distance between your car and the car ahead when:

options.text: You are following a small passenger car.
Another driver is tailgating you.
You are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When tailgated, create extra space in front of your car. Slow down gradually or change lanes to prevent a crash. Do not brake suddenly.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: Avoid slamming on the brakes or making sharp turns in bad weather. Smooth steering and braking help you maintain control of your vehicle.

questions.question: A driver who leaves a gas station without paying will:

options.text: Have their license suspended.
Receive a warning.
Face no consequences.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have their license suspended.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive away from a gas station without paying. Doing this is a serious crime and can result in license suspension after the first conviction.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you:

options.text: Must yield to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
Must yield only to vehicles on your right.
Should slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must yield to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic in the lanes you want to enter. Be ready to stop, but you can proceed if there is no traffic in your way.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming cars.
Increase the distance between you and the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is harder because you cannot see as far. Keep more space between you and the car ahead in case you need to stop. Use your headlights correctly—use high beams when safe and low beams when needed.

questions.question: Unless a different speed is posted, the speed limit on the interstate is:

options.text: 55 mph.
70 mph.
80 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 70 mph.
questions.explanation: The standard interstate speed limit is 70 miles per hour. Follow posted signs if they show a different speed.

questions.question: When traffic moves at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to crash if you:

options.text: Drive a few mph faster than other vehicles.
Stay within that speed range.
Drive a few mph slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within that speed range.
questions.explanation: Adjust your speed to match other traffic (as long as it is within the speed limit). Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Crashes happen when drivers go different speeds.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red traffic light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop, check for traffic or pedestrians, then go.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Stop completely and stay stopped as long as the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, check for traffic or pedestrians, then go.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Stop completely, look for oncoming traffic or pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: A broken yellow center line means:

options.text: You cannot pass.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can cross it to pass on the left if the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: If the rear of your car skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If you skid on a wet or icy road, take your foot off the gas and the brakes. Turn your steering wheel in the direction the rear of the car is sliding. (If you have anti-lock brakes, apply firm brake pressure and steer straight.)
